stem: Simplify $\frac{1}{x+{=p}}+\frac{1}{x+{=q}}$ by writing it as a single fraction.
solution: The denominators are different, so use the common denominator $(x+{=p})(x+{=q})$.
The numerator $2x+{=s}$ has no factor in common with the denominator, so nothing cancels.
notes:
Basic entry point: two unit-numerator fractions with already factorised distinct linear denominators; the numerator never cancels (p,q positive, so 2x+p+q shares no factor). Modelled on bk-exercise-6.
